correctness.rationale: The exact finite-n Gaussian cell mass is q_c(z)=∫_{z+(2c−1)/√n}^{z+(2c+1)/√n}φ(u)du. Shifting s=z+2c/√n gives ∂²_s log q_c=−1+Var_s(T)<0 because T has nondegenerate tilted support [−1/√n,1/√n], so the binomial expectation of −log q_c is strictly convex; binomial reflection makes it even, hence c=0 is uniquely optimal for all n≥1. Independently checking the log interval Taylor coefficients through n^−2, EZ²=1, EZ⁴=3−2/n, EZ⁶=15−30/n+16/n² and the symmetric-binomial entropy H(S_n)=.5 log(π e n/2)−1/(12n²)+o(n^−2) yields D_n(c)=2c²/n+[1/9−(2/3)c²]/n²+o(n^−2) for fixed c. Central-window Taylor bounds and Chernoff-controlled tails justify the expectation. An independent numerical summation for n=200,800,3200 recovers limiting n²D_n(0)→1/9 and nD_n(1/2)→1/2; finite checks alone are not an asymptotic proof.
residual_risks: The claim is restricted to fixed c and symmetric Bin(n,1/2); it does not establish a uniform expansion for c growing with n or nonsymmetric laws.
